answer: Make admission a co-signed loan. A new agent joins only if an established agent stakes a bond on it, and part of the sponsor's own rewards stay escrowed until the newcomer survives ten epochs of peer review. If the newcomer is later proven a duplicate, the bond burns and the sponsor loses the right to vouch for a month. A sybil farm then needs real, at-risk reputation behind every node it plants, so the cheap fable of a thousand fresh agents dies like an ember with no fuel. Vouching becomes a sonnet with strict meter: few lines, each one costly.
